subject: Maths
subtopic: Volume of pyramids, cones and spheres
title: Volume of pyramids, cones and spheres
subtitle: Volume and Surface Area · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can calculate the volume of pyramids, cones and spheres using standard formulae.

key_vocab.definition: A pyramid has a polygon base and triangular faces meeting at an apex. A cone is a circular pyramid. Their volumes are one-third of the corresponding prism or cylinder.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can calculate the volume of pyramids, cones and spheres using standard formulae.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: pyramid -- A pyramid has a polygon base and triangular faces meeting at an apex. A cone is a circular pyramid. Their volumes are one-third of the corresponding prism or cylinder.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Pyramids and cones have volume equal to one-third of the corresponding prism or cylinder. A sphere uses its own formula with r cubed.
V = &frac{1}{3} × base area × h
The &frac{1}{3} factor applies to all pyramids and cones

Key examples:
  ✓ Pyramid: V = &frac{1}{3} × base area × h  (one-third of the prism with same base)
  ✓ Cone: V = &frac{1}{3}πr²h  (one-third of the cylinder)
  ✓ Sphere: V = &frac{4}{3}πr³  (uses radius cubed)
  ✗ Cone V = πr²h  (must include the &frac{1}{3} factor)
  ✗ Sphere V = 4πr²  (that is surface area, not volume)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – square-based pyramid
  Find the volume of a pyramid with a square base of side 6 cm and height 10 cm.
  Base area = 6 × 6 = 36 cm²
  V = &frac{1}{3} × 36 × 10
  = 120 cm³
  120 cm³
  (Find the base area first, then multiply by one-third of the height.)

Example 2 – cone
  Find the volume of a cone with radius 5 cm and height 12 cm. Round to 1 d.p.
  V = &frac{1}{3}πr²h
  = &frac{1}{3} × π × 25 × 12
  = 100π = 314.2 cm³
  314.2 cm³
  (Substitute into the cone formula and evaluate.)

sections.title: Pyramids
sections.content:
Find the volume of each pyramid.

(a) Square base side 4 cm, height 9 cm
(b) Square base side 10 cm, height 12 cm
(c) Rectangular base 6 × 8 cm, height 15 cm
(d) Triangular base area 20 cm², height 9 cm

sections.title: Cones
sections.content:
Find the volume of each cone. Round to 1 d.p.

(a) r = 3 cm, h = 7 cm
(b) r = 4 cm, h = 9 cm
(c) r = 6 cm, h = 10 cm
(d) r = 5 cm, h = 15 cm

sections.title: Spheres
sections.content:
Find the volume of each sphere. Round to 1 d.p.

(a) r = 4 cm
(b) r = 6 cm
(c) r = 10 cm
(d) Diameter 14 cm

sections.title: Hemispheres and composite shapes
sections.content:
Find the volume. Round to 1 d.p.

(a) Hemisphere: r = 5 cm
(b) Hemisphere: r = 8 cm
(c) Cone on top of hemisphere, both r = 3 cm, cone h = 4 cm
(d) Cylinder r = 4, h = 10 plus hemisphere r = 4 on top

sections.title: Mixed volume problems
sections.content:
Solve each problem. Round to 1 d.p. where needed.

(a) Cone: diameter 8 cm, height 12 cm. Volume?
(b) Sphere volume = 288π cm³. Find the radius.
(c) Pyramid base 5 × 5 cm, volume = 75 cm³. Find height.
(d) Cone volume = 150 cm³, height = 10 cm. Find radius to 1 d.p.
(e) How many times bigger is a sphere of radius 6 than one of radius 3?

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Volume of a cone = &frac{1}{3}πr²h
✗ Volume of a cone = πr²h
✓ Volume of a sphere uses r³ (radius cubed)
✗ Doubling the radius of a sphere doubles its volume
✓ A hemisphere volume is half of &frac{4}{3}πr³
